evals.name: booking-resumable-audit
evals.prompt: In a disposable copy of the skill-relative fixture evals/fixtures/persistence-campaign, mutation-audit every active test reached through test/booking.test.mjs. Resolve the fixture relative to this skill folder, never the current working directory, and copy it into a temporary directory before running the campaign. Use one fresh subagent per test and do not trust a test that has not failed. Keep a resumable JSON ledger. This is audit-only: do not strengthen survivors. Preserve all existing worktree changes. The supplied mutation-audit.json is historical example evidence, not evidence of this run; create a fresh ledger for the campaign.
evals.expected_output: A sequential, complete per-test mutation campaign with an established baseline, stable inventory, production-only mutations, exact focused failure/pass evidence, safe restoration, survivor reporting, and an independently validated JSON ledger.
expectations: The workflow establishes a passing untouched baseline and complete active-test inventory before the first mutation.
Each mutation trial uses a fresh subagent and mutation workers are run sequentially in the shared checkout.
A test is classified killed only after an intended focused failure, proven restoration, and passing clean focused rerun.
The ledger preserves invalid and survivor attempts and is updated after every trial.
The workflow does not edit tests to harden survivors because the prompt specifies audit-only mode.
Completion requires every inventoried active test to have a terminal status, a passing final suite, and proven restoration of the pre-campaign state.

evals.name: dirty-worktree-regex-selector-and-resume
evals.prompt: Resume the mutation audit described by ./tmp/payment-suite-mutation-audit.json. The repository already has unrelated user edits. Continue only the pending tests in test/payment.test.ts; one test is named `should preserve r+ mode when reopening`. Use a new worker for each loop. The previous run was interrupted while one entry was marked running. Do not discard or stash anything.
evals.expected_output: An interruption-safe resumption that audits the running entry for residual mutation state, preserves unrelated edits, proves an exact selector for the regex-like name, and continues sequentially without duplicating completed ledger records.
expectations: The workflow investigates the running attempt and verifies or restores its mutation before starting new trials.
Existing completed ledger entries are preserved and only pending or safely recovered targets are processed.
The exact selector escapes or otherwise treats the plus sign literally and proves exactly one test was selected.
Restoration is checked against the pre-existing scoped diff rather than against an assumed clean worktree.
The workflow does not use reset, checkout, clean, or stash to restore files.

evals.name: multi-runtime-blocked-and-survivor-hardening
evals.prompt: Audit the shared FileSystem conformance suite through both its Node and Deno entrypoints. Use one fresh subagent per runtime/test target. Deno may not be installed. Record the audit in filesystem-test-mutation-audit.json. If a test survives, explain the missing observation and strengthen it with deterministic behavior before re-auditing it; avoid sleep-based or negative-timeout assertions.
evals.expected_output: A runtime-aware mutation ledger that does not misclassify unavailable Deno execution, keeps Node and Deno targets distinct, preserves survivor history, and uses a fresh trial to verify any authorized deterministic test strengthening.
expectations: Node and Deno executions are inventoried as distinct targets where runtime behavior can differ.
An unavailable Deno runner is classified blocked and is never reported as passed, survived, or killed.
The workflow records an initial survivor before making an authorized focused test improvement.
Survivor hardening prefers deterministic positive observation over sleeps or negative timeout listeners.
The strengthened test receives a new fresh-worker mutation attempt and the original survivor remains in history.
The final report distinguishes verified results from blocked runtime coverage and does not claim full cross-runtime completion.
